question: Will the French government invoke Article 49.3 on the 2027 finance bill (PLF 2027) before December 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: PLF 2027 rejected at Assembly first reading (458-0, Nov 4); the text is now in the Senate until a Dec 9 vote, the CMP is around mid-December, and the 70-day Art. 47 deadline expires Dec 17 at midnight. A qualifying 49.3 therefore has to land in a narrow Dec ~10-17 slot (on CMP conclusions or at the start of nouvelle lecture). Base rate: 49.3 was used on every PLF 2023-2026, but the decisive 49.3 for PLF 2026 came on Jan 20, 2026, after a special law, i.e. outside the equivalent window. Lecornu made no anti-49.3 pledge this year, the Senate wants gains folded in via 49.3, and MUFG expects 49.3. Against: the executive 'won't rush', is openly keeping ordinances on the table and isn't actively negotiating with the hostile PS ahead of the presidential election, and censure risk makes ordinances or a special law attractive. Market: none matching; the closest is Polymarket 'France passes budget by Dec 31, 2026' at ~45.5% (near-miss contract, ordinances may count, volume unknown), treated as weak evidence only.
calls.dossier:
- PLF 2027 presented to Council of Ministers Oct 1, 2026; tabled ~Oct 9; Assembly debate began Oct 13 (franceinfo; Public Sénat, Nov 3 2026).
- Nov 4, 2026: Assembly rejected the revenue part 458-0, which ends the first reading; the text goes to the Senate (LCP, Nov 5 2026). PLFSS 2027 was rejected 115-1 on Oct 23.
- Senate calendar: PLFSS Nov 9/12-18; PLF debate Nov 20 - Dec 8/9; PLF Senate vote Dec 9. PLF CMP 'around mid-December'. Art. 47 70-day deadline for the PLF: Dec 17, 2026 at midnight; for the PLFSS: Nov 26 (Public Sénat Nov 3; LCP Nov 5).
- After Dec 17 the government may enact the budget by ordinances (never done before); a censure motion would not undo it. A special law extending the 2026 budget is also possible (LCP Nov 5).
- Lecornu made no anti-49.3 pledge for 2027 (unlike 2026). He offered 'neither 49.3 nor ordinances' if LFI doesn't obstruct; an executive source says 'we won't rush' and 'all options open including ordinances' (franceinfo; Europe1).
- Assembly President Braun-Pivet and rapporteur Juvin pushed for an early 49.3 in first reading; it was not done (LCP Nov 2 2026).
- Sud Radio Nov 9 2026: the executive is 'playing patience', not actively negotiating; a compromise search is pencilled for December; the right-wing Senate wants gains incorporated 'via 49.3' to avoid ordinances; PS senators are hostile.
- PS: Faure signalled in late August that censure was likely; deputy Mercier was more open in mid-September (franceinfo). Presidential election April 2027.
- MUFG Research (Oct 2 2026) expects a modified budget passed using 49.3, 'mirroring recent years'.
- Precedents: 49.3 used on PLF 2023, 2024 and 2025 in the autumn (Borne; Barnier's on PLFSS CMP text Dec 2 2024, censured Dec 4). PLF 2026: CMP failed ~Dec 19 2025, special law, then 49.3 x3 from Jan 20 2026 after a PS non-censure deal, i.e. outside a 'before Dec 18' window.
- Resolution: only an actual engagement of responsibility in the Assemblée chamber on PLF 2027 counts; Council of Ministers authorization, statements, ordinances, and PLFSS 49.3 do not.
- Event window: question open -> Dec 18 2026 CET; as of Nov 9 the text is outside the Assembly (in the Senate) until ~Dec 10; feasible 49.3 slot ~Dec 10-17.
- Markets: searched Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi; no matching contract; a looser Polymarket 'budget passed by Dec 31' market exists.
- Not found: any Lecornu statement after Nov 4 on 49.3 timing; an exact CMP date; a PS-government deal.
calls.reference_class: French PLF cycles under a minority government since 2022 (PLF 2023-2026): was 49.3 invoked on the PLF before ~Dec 18?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no 49.3 yet; Assembly rejected PLF 2027 revenue part 458-0 on Nov 4 in first reading, bill to Senate Nov 20-Dec 9, CMP mid-December, 70-day deadline Dec 17 midnight. A 49.3 on CMP conclusions or nouvelle lecture is feasible Dec 10-17 (Borne did so in Dec 2022). Unlike 2025, Lecornu has not renounced 49.3 ('all options open'), rapporteur demands it, Senate expects gains integrated via 49.3. Against: last year CMP failed Dec 19 and 49.3 slipped to January after a special law; ordinances after Dec 17 or a special law are alternatives; PS threatens censure amid pre-presidential positioning; Matignon in wait-and-see mode. Invocation counts even if censured. No human market found.
calls.dossier:
- Nov 4 2026 (LCP, franceinfo, profession-gendarme): Assemblée rejected revenue part of PLF 2027 458-0 (2 abstentions) in first reading, even Ensemble voted against; whole bill thus rejected, goes to Senate in government's original text. No 49.3 used in first reading.
- Calendar (LCP, nosparlementaires, Orange Nov 6): Senate PLFSS Nov 9-18; Senate PLF Nov 20-Dec 9, solemn vote Dec 9; CMP (7+7) from ~Dec 9/mid-December, no official date; if CMP fails, nouvelle lecture both chambers then lecture définitive at Assemblée; 70-day constitutional deadline for PLF expires Dec 17 midnight; special law could be deployed before ~Dec 19; shuttle must end before ~Dec 21.
- Oct 1 2026 (franceinfo): Lecornu team: 'all options remain open, including ordinances'; unlike 2025 he did not pledge to renounce 49.3. A Renaissance deputy suggested using 49.3 quickly.
- Oct 21 2026 (journalducoin): minister Lescure: 'if we go off the road, we'll use the guardrails'; rapporteur général (Juvin) demanding 49.3 since August.
- Nov 9 2026 (Sud Radio): Lecornu has not committed; wait-and-see; Matignon schedules compromise talks for December; options 49.3, ordinances (initial text only, no modifications), or negotiated compromise; right-wing Senate wants to 'avoid ordinances' by getting gains integrated in final copy via 49.3; social anger/student movement context.
- Oct 2026 (echosplus, moneyvox): PS (Faure, Vallaud) calls budget 'not acceptable', maintains censure threat; Lecornu offers compromise like last year. actu-alt-plus claims RN signaled (Nov 5) it might refrain from censure — single source, unverified.
- Precedent: PLF 2026 — Lecornu renounced 49.3 in Oct 2025, CMP failed Dec 19 2025, special law passed before Christmas, then 49.3 invoked in Jan 2026 (first ~Jan 19-20) after PS non-censure deal; censure motions failed. Barnier Dec 2024: 49.3 on PLFSS CMP text Dec 2, government censured Dec 4. Borne 2022-23: multiple 49.3 on PLF in Oct-Dec including nouvelle lecture/lecture définitive in mid-December.
- Ordinances (Art 47) never used under Fifth Republic; legally contested; per nosparlementaires cannot apply if Parliament rejected text.
- Resolution: needs actual engagement of responsibility in the Assemblée chamber on PLF 2027 (any part/any reading); PLFSS 49.3, Council of Ministers authorization, statements, or ordinances do not count. Invocation counts regardless of later censure.
- Event window: question open -> Dec 18 2026 CET; as of Nov 9 roughly 0% of the practically relevant window (Dec 9-17 post-Senate) has elapsed; Assemblée has the text back only after Senate vote Dec 9.
- Searched, absent: official CMP date, Assembly agenda for nouvelle lecture, any explicit Lecornu commitment for or against 49.3 on PLF 2027, PS-government non-censure deal for 2027. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found.
calls.reference_class: Recent French PLF cycles under minority governments (2022-2025): 49.3 used on PLF in 2022, 2023, 2024 (Barnier, PLFSS/PLF Dec), 2025-26 (Jan 2026); timing before Dec 18 in roughly 3 of 4

calls.reasoning: Base rate for a PLF 49.3 before mid-December: 2 of 2 under the 2022-24 relative majority, but 0 of 2 in the hung Assembly since 2024 (2024 and 2025 both went through a special law, with the 49.3 coming in Jan-Feb). The PLF 2027 first reading is over (revenue part rejected 458-0 on Nov 4), so a counting 49.3 needs a new reading, or a vote on a CMP text, in about Dec 11-17, right after the Senate votes on Dec 9 and before the 70-day deadline on Dec 17. Lecornu has publicly said 'no 49.3, no ordinances', but officials keep every option open, and reports say he wants to 'secure the calendar', which raises the odds of a December 49.3. Against that: he needs RN or PS non-censure before the 2027 presidential election, the timetable is tight, and the alternatives (ordinances after Dec 17 or another special law) resolve No. No prediction market was found.
calls.dossier:
- Nov 4 2026: Assembly rejected the PLF 2027 revenue part 458-0, a first under the Fifth Republic. First reading over, bill sent to Senate (LCP, franceinfo, Nov 5).
- Senate calendar: PLFSS Nov 9/12-18; PLF Nov 20 - Dec 8, Senate vote Dec 9. CMP on the PLF 'mid-December'. 70-day PLF deadline expires Dec 17 at midnight; PLFSS deadline about Nov 26 (Public Senat Nov 3; LCP Nov 5).
- After Dec 17 the government may enact the original bill by ordinances (never done before) or pass a special law extending 2026 appropriations. The 2024 and 2025 special laws both led to budgets finalized in February (actu-alt-plus).
- Oct 1 2026 (franceinfo): Lecornu told Le Figaro 'Il n'y aura ni 49.3, ni ordonnances, et à la fin, il y aura un vote !'. An executive source: 'toutes les issues restent ouvertes, y compris la voie des ordonnances'. Unlike 2025, he made no formal pledge to give up 49.3.
- Oct 21: spokesperson Lescure on RTL, 'si on a une sortie de route, on fera jouer les glissières'. Budget rapporteur Philippe Juvin has pushed for 49.3 since August (Journal du Coin).
- Nov 2026 (Sud Radio, Belgium Times Nov 6): Matignon has pushed compromise talks to December, after the Senate. Two scenarios under study: 49.3 or ordinances. Reported aim is to 'sécuriser le calendrier'. Less horse-trading with the PS than in 2025. France's GDP contracted in Q3.
- Censure positions: LFI says it will file censure if 49.3 is used (Le Coq, Oct 9). PS: Faure hardline ('censure would occur'), deputy Estelle Mercier 'open to discussion'. RN: Le Pen says an imperfect budget beats an extended special law, but deputies will judge 'on substance'. Survival needs RN or PS to abstain from censure.
- History: PLF 2023 and PLF 2024 had 49.3s in Oct-Dec (relative majority). PLF 2025: Barnier fell Dec 4 2024 over a PLFSS 49.3; PLF 49.3 came only in Jan-Feb 2025 under Bayrou. PLF 2026: Lecornu gave up 49.3 in Oct 2025 at the PS's request, special law Dec 23 2025, then 49.3s in Jan 2026, budget adopted Feb 2 2026.
- Status quo: no 49.3 has yet been used on the PLF 2027 (first reading ended in a vote).
- Resolves off an actual engagement of responsibility in the Assemblée nationale chamber on the PLF 2027 (any part, any reading), not a Council of Ministers authorization, statements, ordinances, or the PLFSS.
- Event window: question open -> Dec 18 2026 CET. As of Nov 9, a large share has elapsed by calendar, but the only realistic slot is about Dec 10-17 (after the Dec 9 Senate vote and the CMP).
- Searched for but not found: a scheduled date for the Assembly's new reading, any PS/RN non-censure deal, any prediction market (none on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: French PLF cycles 2022-2025: was 49.3 used on the PLF before Dec 18, conditioned on the Assembly having no majority

calls.reasoning: PLF 2027 first reading ended without 49.3 (revenue part rejected 458-0 Nov 4). Senate debates Nov 20-Dec 9; CMP mid-December; 70-day deadline Dec 17. A qualifying 49.3 must land ~Dec 10-17 on the CMP text or a new reading, which is feasible (Borne did it Dec 15, 2022). Lecornu's 'ni 49.3 ni ordonnances' is conditional on no LFI obstruction and officials keep all options open; the Senate wants gains folded in via 49.3. Against: in both hung-Assembly years (PLF 2025, PLF 2026) the 49.3 came only in Jan-Feb after a special law; censure risk before the April 2027 presidential election; ordinances, a special law or a negotiated vote all resolve No. No matching market found.
calls.reconciliation: Factual disputes: (1) whether Lecornu pledged against 49.3. Search confirmed he said 'ni 49.3, ni ordonnances... il y aura un vote', but conditional on no LFI obstruction, with officials keeping all options open: a soft, conditional pledge, not a formal renunciation as in 2025. (2) Calendar: confirmed Senate Nov 20-Dec 9, compromise talks deferred to December, 70-day deadline Dec 17; no CMP date found. (3) Senate stance: confirmed Mouiller wants gains incorporated via 49.3. No new facts on a PS/RN deal; no market found beyond the runs' reports. The remaining dispute is judgment: how much the hung-Assembly precedent (49.3 slipping to January after a special law) weighs against deadline pressure and the soft pledge. I weight that precedent heavily, which puts me just below Run 1.

disagreements.verdict: Partly true: 'ni 49.3 ni ordonnances' conditional on no LFI obstruction; options officially kept open; softer than the 2025 pledge
